To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nerve growth factor and epidermal growth factors induce a series of rapid surface changes in PC12 cells which include the appearance of dorsal ruffles, peripheral ruffles, blebbing, and an increased density of coated pits.
NGF, EGF, and dibutyrl cyclic AMP induce a series of surface changes in PC12 cells that are similar to those observed for NGF in sympathetic neurons.
NGF and EFG induce rapid changes in cell morphology and coated pit density in PC12 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of NGF.

the mechanisms of action of nerve growth factor (and other growth factors/hormone peptides) in normal sympathetic neurons and PC12 cells, a pheochromcytoma cell line derived from the rat adrenal medulla which is known to respond to NGF in a manner similar to the normal cells.
the mechanism by which nerve growth factor (and possibly other growth factors/hormone) act on cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cell surface changes described here are not specific for NGF, but rather are a common response to a wide variety of growth factors and hormones.
the surface changes are the result of a complex interplay of factors which include the growth factor, its receptor, the cell membrane and its components, and the cytoskeleton.
NGF, EGF, and dibutylyl cyclic AMP induce different responses in PC12 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the surface changes induced in PC12 cells by NGF, EGF, or a combined treatment with both factors, and the increase in coated pit density, are all rapid, reversible, and specific responses of PC12 cells to these factors and are not caused by dibutyryl cAMP.
NGF and EFG cause similar surface changes in PC12 cells.

NGF, EGF, and dibutylyl cyclic AMP cause a series of surface responses in PC12 cells which are different in time course but similar in morphology, and that these responses are associated with the appearance of a large number of coated pits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NGF and EFG are very similar, and the main difference is in the time it takes to reach the maximum.
NGF and EFG have the same rapid effects on the surface of the cells, and that the effects of NGF are reduced when cells are pretreated with NGF.
the surface changes are rapid and are not dependent on new protein synthesis, and that the surface response to NGF and EFG are very similar.
